observation_summary: The system throws an IllegalFieldValueException when performing arithmetic on a MonthDay object set to February 29th, because the underlying logic attempts to validate the date against a non-leap year (1970).
hypothesis: The bug is caused by an incorrect handling of the leap day (February 29th) when performing arithmetic operations on a MonthDay object. The current implementation in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add attempts to reconstruct the date by setting fields on a zero-based instant, which fails because the default year (1970) is not a leap year, causing the day-of-month 29 to be invalid for February.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a special case in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add to handle MonthDay objects specifically, avoiding the conversion to a non-leap-year instant when the operation involves the month field.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace and the provided fix diff confirm that the logic in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add is insufficient for handling leap-day-related partials. The fix introduces a specific branch to handle month-based arithmetic for MonthDay objects, which is a procedural correction to the algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The failure occurs because the code assumes a generic way to add time to partials, which fails for leap days when the underlying chronology defaults to a non-leap year. The fix adds a specific algorithmic path for MonthDay objects to correctly calculate the new month without triggering invalid date exceptions.
